grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a basic staple: lamb mince, cabbage, celeriac, eggs, flour, oil, yoghurt, lemon and cumin.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a grater and a bowl, and shallow-frying spoonfuls is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Three eggs and 100g flour bind the 550g of finely shredded and grated veg plus the lamb, and thin fritters at 3 minutes a side will cook through; any cook will see they need to fry in batches.

honest_times.reason: The mix makes around 16 fritters, so the lamb's 8 minutes plus about three batches at 6 minutes each runs to roughly 26 minutes of hands-on frying, well past the 15 unattended cook minutes printed for a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon zest and juice, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Hot, filling fritters suit a cold February lunch, and 300g of shredded white cabbage is a main component, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and plainly worded in British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lamb, eggs and plenty of veg with a yoghurt dip make a proper, satisfying family lunch.
